summary.headline: Sigachi Q2 FY27 revenue INR 130.45 cr with 14.72% EBITDA margin; management trims FY27 revenue target from INR 650 cr to about INR 600 cr.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total operating income was INR 130.45 crore, with EBITDA of INR 19.2 crore (14.72% margin) and net profit of INR 8.78 crore (6.82% margin). MCC contributed INR 91.22 crore, O&M INR 13.93 crore and API INR 16.67 crore. Management cut its full-year revenue expectation to about INR 600 crore (stretch INR 600 crore, comfortable INR 550-575 crore) from INR 650 crore, citing deferred commissioning of the 12,000 MTPA MCC expansion. Utilisation was about 80% across Dahej and Jhagadia, and the INR 200 crore preferential issue was called off.

financial_highlights.value: About 7,128 MT produced and sold for H1 (about 3,700 MT in Q2)

segments.name: MCC (excipients)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 91.22 crore, about 70% of total; described by management as the cash cow. Utilisation about 80% (Dahej ~80%, Jhagadia ~79%) in H1.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 16.67 crore; H1 about INR 35-40 crore. Current capacity 100 kL; management sees up to INR 100 crore, and INR 120-150 crore with value-added products. H1 order book about INR 38 crore.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 13.93 crore, about 11% of revenue; management expects steady 10-12% contribution.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target trimmed to about INR 600 crore (stretch), from INR 650 crore; INR 550-575 crore described as more easily achievable. The cut reflects deferral of the MCC 12,000 MTPA expansion.

FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of about 18% retained; H2 margin expected at or above 18%, versus about 15% currently, helped by fixed overheads being flat and a richer mix of special and co-processed grades.

MCC 12,000 MTPA expansion at Dahej SEZ expected in Q2 FY28 (maybe 1-2 months slippage), taking total MCC capacity to about 30,000 MTPA. Management estimated around INR 243 crore of incremental annual revenue from it (12,000 MT at INR 250 and 10,800 MT operated at INR 225).
MCC production targeted at about 4,500 MT per quarter by Q4 FY27; capacity additions expected to be commissioned by November 15 to 20, 2026.

CCS facility at Dahej also expected to commercialise in Q2 FY28. CapEx for MCC and CCS is about INR 200 crore in total (about INR 100 crore MCC, about INR 90 crore CCS), with INR 29-30 crore spent so far.
Insurance reimbursement of about INR 49 crore expected by November or December 2026, with about 10% discount indicated.
capex_capacity: MCC capacity to rise from about 18,000 to about 30,000 MTPA with the 12,000 MTPA Dahej SEZ expansion (Q2 FY28). Total spent on MCC and CCS so far is about INR 29-30 crore.

Utilisation in H1 was about 80%, lowered by safety equipment retrofits to FBDs and dryers after the Hyderabad plant accident; management says the remaining equipment will be installed by November 2026.
API capacity is 100 kL; current products are sparsentan and bempedoic acid, which carry higher margins.

Funding: internal accruals and the insurance receivable are the immediate sources. Debt or equity for the rest is not finalised; the INR 200 crore preferential issue was called off, though management says a preferential issue is not ruled out.
Most CapEx equipment is sourced domestically. Plant and machinery orders are to be placed in the next 2-3 months, with about one year to completion.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is very high and orders exceed production; supply is the binding constraint, and it sees no pricing pressure from competitors running near full capacity.

Realisations rose to INR 262.83 per tonne in Q2 from INR 241.36 in Q1, driven by sales mix toward special and co-processed grades; management says normal-versus-co-processed mix shifts are expected to lift H2 realisations further.
Management said some API revenue slipped from Q2 into Q3 because customers asked for later dispatch; API H2 target is about INR 100 crore, with up to INR 120 crore possible.

qa_highlights.question: Are you sticking to the INR 650 crore revenue and 18% EBITDA guidance given H1 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue trimmed to about INR 600 crore because the MCC expansion slipped; H2 margin is expected at or above 18% as fixed costs are flat and mix improves.

qa_highlights.question: Can H2 revenue rise about 40% over H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites better utilisation (about 10% uplift from mid-November), API ramp-up and O&M growth; it did not give a quarterly bridge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the API capacity and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: 100 kL capacity, potentially INR 100 crore revenue, INR 120-150 crore with value-added products. H1 order book INR 38 crore; INR 100 crore expected for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 200 crore preferential issue called off?
qa_highlights.answer: Investor feedback on the INR 26.4 pricing, with the stock then trading near INR 39, led promoters to cancel the issue; a fundraise remains open through debt or equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why is utilisation only about 80% despite strong demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Safety retrofits after the Hyderabad accident, including FBD and dryer equipment, required shutting down units one by one. Management expects full utilisation after the final installation in November.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex funding plan and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Total about INR 200 crore (MCC about INR 100 crore, CCS about INR 90 crore) with roughly one year to completion; debt or equity mix not finalised.

risks_watch: Revenue execution: H2 needs about 40% growth over H1 (about INR 250 crore to about INR 350 crore) to reach INR 600 crore, and the analyst's own estimate was INR 550 crore.
Repeated project slippage: the MCC expansion moved from Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28, and CCS commercialisation is also in Q2 FY28.
Funding gap of about INR 200 crore for CapEx after the preferential issue was called off; the final mix of debt, equity and insurance proceeds is open.
Insurance receivable of about INR 49 crore, subject to a 5-10% discount and timing uncertainty, with the surveyor and insurer discussions ongoing.
Utilisation remains about 80% while safety retrofits continue; full run-rate depends on completing installations in November 2026.
API order flow lumpy: revenue deferred from Q2 to Q3 by customer request.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and margin recovery, but cautious on timing: management trimmed the revenue target and repeatedly qualified its timelines ("one or two months here and there"). It was evasive on funding, deferring the debt-versus-equity decision to a future announcement.
key_quotes: Now, more or less, around INR 600 or so we can reach. In this, there would be a little slip.
We have high demand, right now, the supply is the only constraint.

adds.what: 12,000 MTPA MCC expansion at Dahej SEZ (total MCC to ~30,000 MTPA)

growth.why: FY27 revenue target trimmed from INR 650 cr to about INR 600 cr (INR 550-575 cr comfortable) on deferral of the 12,000 MTPA MCC expansion to Q2 FY28; H1 turnover about INR 250 cr, with API H2 target ~INR 100 cr backed by an H1 order book of ~INR 38 cr and H2 margin guided at or above 18%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides H2 EBITDA margin at or above 18% versus about 15% in H1, citing flat fixed overheads and a richer mix of special and co-processed grades; FY27 margin guide of about 18% retained.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 12,000 MTPA MCC expansion at Dahej SEZ, taking total MCC to about 30,000 MTPA (from about 18,000), has slipped from Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28 with possible 1-2 months more; about INR 29-30 cr of the roughly INR 200 cr MCC+CCS capex spent so far.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: MCC output targeted at about 4,500 MT per quarter by Q4 FY27 versus about 3,700 MT in Q2; utilisation about 80% with roughly 10% uplift expected from mid-November, and management says orders exceed production.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% and the MCC+CCS capex of about INR 200 cr is still being funded (INR 200 cr preferential issue called off, debt or equity mix not finalised), with plant and machinery orders to be placed in the next 2-3 months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue was cut from INR 650 cr to about INR 600 cr (comfortable INR 550-575 cr), and H2 needs about 40% growth over H1 (about INR 250 cr to INR 350 cr) to reach it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Repeated slippage (MCC expansion moved from Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28, CCS also Q2 FY28) and H2 revenue needs about 40% step-up, while an analyst estimate was INR 550 cr.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CCS facility at Dahej to commercialise in Q2 FY28 (about INR 90 cr capex) and API value-added products could lift API to INR 120-150 cr, but neither has a firm launch date.

rows.label: API order book and H2 ramp
rows.why: H1 API order book about INR 38 cr and H2 API target about INR 100 cr (up to INR 120 cr), with some Q2 revenue deferred into Q3 at customer request.

rows.label: Insurance reimbursement of about INR 49 cr
rows.why: Expected by November or December 2026 with about a 10% discount indicated (5-10% range), giving a cash inflow toward the INR 200 cr capex.

rows.label: Safety retrofits completed, utilisation recovers
rows.why: Remaining FBD and dryer safety equipment to be installed by November 2026, after which management expects about 10% utilisation uplift and full run-rate from current ~80%.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing and the H2 margin recovery to at least 18%, but cautious on timing, trimming the revenue target and repeatedly qualifying timelines, and evasive on the debt-versus-equity funding mix for the INR 200 cr capex. Analysts pressed on the roughly 40% H2 revenue
